clue.text: Affair makes the woman explode

parts.note: a female person referred to as she
to explode is to go bang

explanation.surface: A love affair causes a woman to blow up in anger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The whole shebang' is an idiom for the entire business, so SHEBANG can stand for an affair or matter.
explanation.definitionFit: Shebang is an informal word for a matter or business, as in 'the whole shebang'.

clue.text: Small host putting everyone off, being obsequious

indicators.note: putting ... off, split around the word removed, says those letters are taken away
with putting, signals that the word for everyone is dropped from the word before

parts.note: taken as written
everyone means all
a host is a great multitude, especially an army

explanation.surface: A minor host who drives away all the guests by fawning over them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'putting ... off' removes ALL from SMALL, leaving SM; add ARMY. 'Small' looks like the S abbreviation but is used whole.
explanation.definitionFit: Smarmy describes oily, ingratiating behaviour, a near synonym of fawning servility.

clue.text: Bits chucked out from back of the plane keeping maximum speed over top of Alps

indicators.note: back of picks the final letter of the word the
keeping means one piece holds the other inside it

parts.note: a jet is a kind of aeroplane
c, the speed of light, is the highest speed possible in physics

indicators.note: top of picks the first letter of the word Alps

explanation.surface: Debris falls from the tail of a fast jet flying over mountains.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' is a link: in this down clue the pieces stack above the A from Alps.
explanation.definitionFit: Ejecta is matter thrown out, as from a volcano, so it is a word for material expelled.

clue.text: Expecting awful panic stations, sending out SOS

indicators.note: awful says the letters are in a terrible mess, rearranged
sending out says the letters of SOS are removed from the jumble

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Anticipating dreadful scenes of alarm, someone stops sending distress signals.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove S, O and S from PANICSTATIONS and rearrange what is left. The answer is used adjectivally: someone anticipant is expecting.
explanation.definitionFit: Anticipant is an adjective meaning looking forward to or awaiting something, so it matches waiting in hope.

clue.text: Some gaga person who has their mouth wide open?

definitions.text: who has their mouth wide open

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A doddery person standing with jaw hanging in amazement.
explanation.definitionFit: A gaper is someone who stares open-mouthed, gawping in astonishment.

clue.text: Derby? Somewhat limited as a place in which to live

definitions.text: a place in which to live

indicators.note: limited means held within bounds, so one piece encloses the other

parts.note: a derby is a bowler hat
somewhat means a bit

explanation.surface: Derby as a town seems a rather cramped place to live.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Derby' looks like the English city or the horse race, but it is the hat.
explanation.definitionFit: A habitat is the natural home or surroundings of an animal or plant.

clue.text: The fellow managed to include ridiculous clue, fiendishly difficult

parts.note: a man referred to as he

indicators.note: to include means one piece is placed inside another

parts.note: to manage a business is to run it, past tense ran

indicators.note: ridiculous says the letters are made absurd, rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A crossword solver beat a silly, devilish clue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ridiculous' looks like a judgement on the clue, but it is the anagram signal; 'fiendishly' is part of the definition, not another one.
explanation.definitionFit: Herculean, after the labours of Hercules, means requiring enormous effort.

clue.text: Mistake is nonsense — rub out

indicators.note: out tells us the word rub is taken out of the word for nonsense

parts.note: nonsense means rubbish
taken as written

explanation.surface: An error is pure nonsense, so erase it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rub out' reads as erase, but 'rub' is the letters removed and 'out' the instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: Bish is British slang for a blunder or error.

clue.text: Left in south London district, going here and there

indicators.note: in means one piece goes inside another

parts.note: Tooting is a district in south London

explanation.surface: Someone abandoned in a corner of south London, wandering about.
explanation.walkthrough: TOOTING is an area of south-west London.
explanation.definitionFit: Tootling means wandering or driving about in a leisurely, aimless way.

clue.text: Divine government offered by those people roguish inside

indicators.note: inside places one piece within the other

parts.note: a group referred to as they
arch means mischievous or roguish

explanation.surface: Rule by the gods, offered by a mischievous crew.
explanation.definitionFit: Thearchy is rule by a god or gods, theocracy in its literal sense.

clue.text: Expert in a small part of the organisation

parts.note: dept is the short form of department, a section of an organisation

explanation.surface: A specialist working in one corner of a company.
explanation.definitionFit: Adept as a noun is a skilled practitioner, a master of some field.

clue.text: Fairies cope — such may help little folk to have a vision

definitions.text: such may help little folk to have a vision

parts.note: peris are fairies in Persian mythology
taken as written

explanation.surface: Magical beings manage, using an instrument that lets the small see over obstacles.
explanation.walkthrough: A peri is a Persian fairy; 'little folk' are short people, not fairies.
explanation.definitionFit: A periscope lets someone see over a barrier, so a short person can see past a crowd.

clue.text: Came across a fish with useless bones

parts.note: to come across someone is to meet them, past tense met
a carp is a freshwater fish
US is the abbreviation for unserviceable, meaning useless

explanation.surface: Discovered a fish whose bones are inedible.
explanation.definitionFit: The metacarpus is the set of five hand bones between wrist and fingers.

clue.text: Slight indication of inebriation?

definitions.meaning: a slight as a noun is an insult or aspersion

explanation.definitionFit: A slur is both a disparaging remark and a blurred way of speaking, as when drunk.

clue.text: Time to have water carried up, lights out all around? Now do this!

indicators.note: all around says the jumbled letters surround the rest
out says the letters are out of order, rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: carried up in a down clue means the pieces are read upwards, backwards

parts.note: pee is slang for urine, making water

explanation.surface: A bedtime scene: a drink of water taken up, lights off, and a parting instruction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Now do this!' is the definition: the phrase is the instruction itself, said at bedtime, which the rest of the clue pictures.
explanation.definitionFit: Sleep tight is what one says at bedtime, an instruction to rest well.

clue.text: Provisions for picnic? Spooner's didn't include spicy drink

indicators.note: Spooner swapped the starting sounds of words, so the initial consonants of two words change places

parts.note: to lack something is not to have it, past tense lacked
punch is a mixed drink often spiced

explanation.surface: A picnic hamper that lacked any spiced punch.
explanation.definitionFit: A packed lunch is food prepared to take out and eat away from home.

clue.text: That woman in castle, finally, after cruel act?

definitions.text: That woman in castle, finally, after cruel act?

indicators.note: after says the following pieces come behind the jumbled letters
cruel says the letters are treated roughly, rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
a female person referred to as her
taken as written

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of the word castle

explanation.surface: A queen confined in a castle after a cruel deed.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue points to queens such as Catherine of Aragon, confined at Kimbolton Castle, or the Catherine wheel torture.
explanation.definitionFit: Catherine of Aragon, a woman cruelly set aside and kept in a castle, fits the clue's picture.

clue.text: Regret the absence of embracing very French inamorata

indicators.note: embracing means holding the other piece inside

parts.note: to miss someone is to regret their absence
tres is French for very

explanation.surface: Sorry to be without a hug from one's French lover.
explanation.definitionFit: A mistress is a female lover, the same idea as an inamorata.

clue.text: Drama half way through — a break gives space for this?

definitions.text: Drama half way through — a break gives space for this?

indicators.note: through means one piece passes inside the other

parts.note: a break is a pause

indicators.note: half takes the first two of the four letters

parts.note: a drama is a play

explanation.surface: Midway through a play, the interval gives room for clapping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'way' is only a link here; applause at an interval is the scene the whole clue paints.
explanation.definitionFit: Audiences clap during breaks in a performance, so the pause makes room for it.

clue.text: Remorselessness shown by pet with nine mice being destroyed

indicators.note: being destroyed says these letters are broken up and rebuilt

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A cat kills nine mice without any regret.
explanation.definitionFit: Impenitence is the state of feeling no regret, the lack of contrition.

clue.text: Guide said he decided to go with the crowd

definitions.text: he decided to go with the crowd

indicators.note: said means spoken, so the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: a pilot guides ships or aircraft

explanation.surface: A guide claimed that he followed popular opinion.
explanation.walkthrough: Pontius Pilate yielded to the crowd, releasing Barabbas.
explanation.definitionFit: Pontius Pilate let the crowd choose Barabbas over Jesus, bowing to public demand.

clue.text: Be unable to bear endless study prior to exam?

indicators.note: endless means the final letter is removed

parts.note: a den is a private study
an exam is a test

explanation.surface: Hating the cramming before an exam that never ends.
explanation.definitionFit: To detest is to loathe, to find something intolerable.

clue.text: Command man with a bow

definitions.meaning: to order someone to do something
William ..., the Swiss archer of legend

explanation.definitionFit: Tell can mean order, and William Tell was the legendary crossbowman.

clue.text: Careerist working to escape finally from desk

indicators.note: working says the letters are being worked into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of the word escape

explanation.surface: An ambitious employee trying to break away from the office desk.
explanation.definitionFit: A secretaire is a writing desk with drawers, a type of bureau.

clue.text: Approach game with attempt at humour taken the wrong way

parts.note: RU is rugby union

indicators.note: taken the wrong way says the word is read backwards

parts.note: a pun is a joke on words

explanation.surface: A sporting event with a joke that gets misunderstood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken the wrong way' suggests offence; it reverses PUN to NUP.
explanation.definitionFit: A run-up is the approach a bowler or jumper makes, or a lead-in period.

clue.text: Estonian composer demonstrates piano technique

parts.note: p is the musical abbreviation for piano, soft
art means skill or technique

explanation.surface: A Baltic composer shows off keyboard skill.
explanation.walkthrough: Arvo Pärt is a contemporary Estonian composer.
explanation.definitionFit: Arvo Pärt is a celebrated Estonian composer of sacred minimalism.

clue.text: To a dunce I may seem inappropriate

definitions.text: To a dunce I may seem inappropriate

indicators.note: inappropriate says the letters are out of place, rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A slow pupil confesses that learning seems pointless.
explanation.definitionFit: Schooling is what a dunce would think pointless, so the whole clue describes it.

clue.text: Cricketer offering a few words at the dinner?

definitions.meaning: W G ..., the great Victorian English cricketer

definitions.text: a few words at the dinner
definitions.meaning: a short prayer said before a meal

explanation.definitionFit: W G Grace was a famous cricketer, and grace is a prayer of thanks before eating.

clue.text: Pony that is taken on by sanctuary without hesitation

indicators.note: without means the following letters are left out

parts.note: a shelter is a place of refuge
er is the sound of hesitating
ie is the abbreviation for id est, that is

explanation.surface: A pony that is taken in at once by an animal refuge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken on by' is a link meaning attached after; ER is the British spelling of a hesitation sound (American 'uh').
explanation.definitionFit: A sheltie is a Shetland pony (or sheepdog).

clue.text: Job was clear — Pasquale gets stuck in

indicators.note: gets stuck in means put inside the other piece

parts.note: patent means obvious, clear
the setter Pasquale is the I who wrote the clue

explanation.surface: The work was obvious, so the setter got down to it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Job' looks like work; it is the biblical Job, famous for patience.
explanation.definitionFit: The biblical Job was proverbially long-suffering, the model of patience.
